name: source-cards
description: Does the answer present a set of real, linkable items as a SourceCards spec block when the user asks to find or collect them, and skip it otherwise? Search results are fixed. A listing item asks for several real things that each have their own page in the fixture. An other item asks for an explanation, steps, a comparison, a single fact, or writing, where cards would be misuse. Fixture URLs use real-looking hosts because a model reasonably refuses to present placeholder .example links as genuine items; job and clinic entries use fictional organizations. Queries are written for the eval in the shape of common production requests, not copied from user data. A roundup item has only articles that mention items, never an item's own page, so cards would link to articles: the expected answer has none. nonItemUrls lists every result that is not an item's own page; it is used for scoring and never shown to the model.

tunnel-spalling-papers.title: Spalling failure around deep tunnels in brittle rock: a field and numerical study
tunnel-spalling-papers.content: Tunnelling and Underground Space Technology, 2025. Combines field observations from a 1,500 m deep tunnel with discrete element modelling to predict spalling depth in granite.

tunnel-spalling-papers.title: Stress-driven spalling in hard rock: a review of prediction criteria
tunnel-spalling-papers.content: Rock Mechanics and Rock Engineering, 2024. Reviews empirical and numerical criteria for spalling onset and compares their accuracy across 40 case histories.

tunnel-spalling-papers.title: Acoustic emission monitoring of spalling in a brittle rock excavation
tunnel-spalling-papers.content: International Journal of Rock Mechanics and Mining Sciences, 2026. Uses acoustic emission sensors to detect micro-cracking before visible spalling.

tunnel-spalling-papers.title: What is rock spalling?
tunnel-spalling-papers.content: Spalling is the breaking off of rock slabs from an excavation surface under high stress, common in hard, brittle rocks such as granite.

sky-blue.title: Why is the sky blue? | NASA Space Place
sky-blue.content: Sunlight is made of many colours. Gas molecules scatter shorter blue wavelengths much more than red ones, a process called Rayleigh scattering, so blue light reaches our eyes from all directions.

sky-blue.title: Rayleigh scattering - Physics explained
sky-blue.content: Scattering intensity is inversely proportional to the fourth power of wavelength, so blue light at 450 nm scatters about 5.5 times more than red light at 700 nm.

sky-blue.title: Why sunsets are red
sky-blue.content: At sunset light travels through more atmosphere, so most blue is scattered away and reds and oranges remain.

python-venv-macos.title: venv - Creation of virtual environments | Python docs
python-venv-macos.content: Create a virtual environment with python3 -m venv .venv, then activate it on macOS with source .venv/bin/activate. Run deactivate to leave it.

python-venv-macos.title: Installing packages using pip and virtual environments
python-venv-macos.content: After activating the environment, install packages with python -m pip install requests. Use pip freeze > requirements.txt to record dependencies.

python-venv-macos.title: Install Python on macOS with Homebrew
python-venv-macos.content: brew install python installs the latest Python 3, which includes the venv module.

berlin-wall.content: The Berlin Wall fell on 9 November 1989, when East German authorities opened the border crossings.

berlin-wall.title: Berlin Wall - Encyclopedia
berlin-wall.content: Built in 1961, the Berlin Wall divided East and West Berlin until 9 November 1989. Formal demolition began in 1990.

autumn-coffee-caption.content: Short captions with a question or call to action and two to five relevant hashtags tend to perform best.

mrna-vaccines.title: How mRNA vaccines work | CDC
mrna-vaccines.content: mRNA vaccines deliver instructions that teach cells to make a harmless piece of a viral protein. The immune system recognizes the protein and builds antibodies. The mRNA breaks down within days and never enters the cell nucleus.

mrna-vaccines.title: Lipid nanoparticles in mRNA delivery
mrna-vaccines.content: Lipid nanoparticles protect fragile mRNA and help it enter cells, where ribosomes translate it into protein.

mrna-vaccines.title: mRNA vaccine history
mrna-vaccines.content: Decades of research on modified nucleosides made mRNA vaccines stable enough for clinical use.

fridge-mold.title: How to clean mold from a refrigerator gasket
fridge-mold.content: Use a solution of one part white vinegar to one part water or diluted dish soap. Avoid undiluted bleach on rubber seals because it can dry and crack them.

fridge-mold.title: Mold cleanup in your home | EPA
fridge-mold.content: Scrub mold off hard surfaces with detergent and water and dry completely. Never mix bleach with ammonia or other cleaners.

fridge-mold.title: Is 70% isopropyl alcohol effective against mold?
fridge-mold.content: 70% isopropyl alcohol kills surface mold on non-porous materials but does not remove stains.

ai-news-explainer.title: What is retrieval-augmented generation?
ai-news-explainer.content: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) retrieves relevant documents at query time and passes them to a language model, so answers can cite current sources instead of relying only on training data.

ai-news-explainer.title: RAG vs fine-tuning
ai-news-explainer.content: RAG updates knowledge without retraining; fine-tuning changes model behaviour and style. Many systems combine both.

ai-news-explainer.title: Vector databases explained
ai-news-explainer.content: Vector databases store embeddings so a RAG system can find passages similar in meaning to the query.
